This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to FIR No. 683/2023 dated 25/09/2023, registered at Police Station- Amla District Betul for the offence under Sections 363,366, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of IPC and Sections 3/4 and 5L/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
He is in detention since 03/10/2023.

2 . Applicant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed with liberty to renew the prayer for bail after proxecutrix's evidence before the trial Court vide order dated 16/02/2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.3647/2024.

sentences.text: A s per the prosecution story, on 25/09/2023, prosecutrix mother informed police that her 15 years old daughter is a student of class 9th.
On 22/09/2023, at around 8:00 a.m., she had left for school by bus for taking examination.

In the evening her daughter made a call from mobile No.
7489737949 to her brother and informed that mobile No. 7489737949 is of her friend and switched off mobile.
She thought that she would be back on Saturday after closing of the school, but she did not come back.
When she made a call on the mobile of her friend, she informed that she is not with her and she will be back on Monday.
Her daughter is missing.
FIR and missing report was registered.
On 01/10/2023, the girl was recovered from the possession of the present applicant.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed for commission of the aforesaid offences.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
The applicant is 18 years old young boy and at the time of commission of alleged offence, he was below 18 years of age.

He and prosecutrix both were having love affairs and they both had gone to visit Balajipuram Temple and from there they proceeded to Bhopal and stayed at Guna and from there they reached Rajasthan, where police arrested them.
It is submitted that the applicant and the prosecutrix both are juvenile and they out of romantic love relations established physical relations.
Applicant has no criminal background.
Prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant.

6 . Considering the fact that the prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court and there is no possibility of influencing of the prosecution witnesses and tempering with the prosecution evidence and having taking into consideration the age of both prosecutrix and applicant and the factum of love relationship between them, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pretrial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant- Rajesh be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE skt Rajesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93642341/
